To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temperature dependence of jth for a double-heterojunction laser is determined by the height of the potential barrier in the heterojunction, the electron lifetime in active region, the electron diffusion lengths, the thickness of the active region, the band gaps of materials forming the heterojunction ΔEg, and the electron surface recombination rate at the heterointeface.
the threshold current of an injection laser depends on the potential barrier height of the heterojuctioon.

the temperature dependence of threshold current of a double-hetero-structure laser is determined by the height of the potential barrier between the active and passive layers, and that this barrier height is the difference between the conduction band edges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temperature dependence of jth(T) for a heterojunction with a potential barrier of finite height, which can be described by the expression jth(T) = Aexp(T/T1) + B exp(T/T2).
the influence of the heterobarrier height in a heterostructure laser on its temperature dependence.
the influence of the potential barrier in a heterojucton laser on the temperature depencence of the threshold current.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory presented here is able to account quantitatively for the temperature dependence jth(T) of the threshold current density of a heterojuction laser.
the temperature dependence of jth(T) in a heterojuction laser is determined by the height of the potential barrier at the heterointeface.

the influence of the potential barrier of height ΔEg in a heterojuction laser on the temperature depence jth( T ) can be explained only if one assumes the existence of a nonradiative recombination channel for the electrons in the active layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the leakage of carriers through the heterobarrier of the active layer is the main factor in determining the temperature dependence of jth in a heterojjunction laser.
the temperature dependence of jth(T) is determined primarily by leakage of electrons through the heterobarrier and by the surface recombination of electrons at the heterointereface.

the leakage of carriers through the heterobarrier of a heterojuction laser and their recombination at the interface are the main causes of the temperature dependence of jth(T) in the temperature range 77–300°K.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature dependence of jth for heterojunction lasers is determined by the leakage current through a heterojunction barrier of height ΔEg.
the temperature dependence of threshold current of heterojunction lasers can be used to obtain information about the parameters of the laser heterojunction.

the leakage through the heterobarrier and the surface recombination at a heterointerface can be neglected in the temperature range 77–300 K for InGaP–InP lasers with Δ = 100 meV and for AlxGa1–xAlyGa1–xA lasers with Δ = ~200 meV.
